topic: Strait of Hormuz oil tanker explosions
headline_marked: [[Two oil tankers exploded]] in Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, Iran claims
headline: Two oil tankers exploded in Strait of Hormuz after hitting mines, Iran claims
summary: Iran's IRGC Navy claims two oil tankers exploded after hitting mines while traversing an unauthorized path in the Strait of Hormuz. This incident heightens concerns over the safety of the critical global shipping lane.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claims two oil tankers exploded after hitting mines while sailing through an unauthorized path in the Strait of Hormuz. This information was reported by Iranian state media on Sunday.
The IRGC Navy asserts that the vessels did not use the designated authorized route for passage through the strait. They allege the explosions occurred when the ships struck mines planted in the sea.
Specific details regarding the names of the ships, their flag countries, or any casualties or damages have not been disclosed. The veracity of these claims could not be immediately verified.

Iran has imposed restrictions on ship movement through the Strait of Hormuz since the start of its conflict with the United States and Israel, directing vessels to use specific paths. There have been previous reports of attacks on ships operating without permission.

Concurrently, the United States has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, contributing to uncertainty for commercial shipping in this vital waterway. Incidents of mine attacks on ships in the strait have reportedly increased in recent days.

Last Friday, 25 sailors were rescued by Oman's navy from a commercial ship that caught fire after being attacked near the Musandam coast, close to the Strait of Hormuz. The day before, Iran's military reported that four oil tankers caught fire after mine explosions while attempting to pass through the strait's unauthorized southern route.
The IRGC statement on the earlier incident noted that the first three ships had turned off their radar and navigation systems. They also reportedly ignored warnings issued by the Iranian navy.

topic: Russia arrests teen for Moscow attack plot
headline_marked: [[Russia arrests teenager planning Moscow park attack]] after US warning
headline: Russia arrests teenager planning Moscow park attack after US warning
summary: The teenager was detained following a US security alert about a potential mass casualty event at Tsaritsyno Museum Park. The suspect had posted images with a weapon and military-style clothing on TikTok.
details: Russia detained a teenager suspected of planning an attack on a popular Moscow park, acting on a warning from the United States. The Federal Security Service (FSB) reported the arrest, which followed a US embassy security alert.

The suspect, a Russian national, had posted photos on TikTok wearing a mask and military-style clothing, holding a weapon. The teenager also shared images of the Tsaritsyno Museum Park grounds, captioning one, "Found a place."

During a search of the teenager's home, the clothing and equipment seen in the photos were recovered. An examination of the suspect's phone revealed searches related to terrorist attacks and mass killings, and a subscription to a neo-Nazi Telegram channel.

The US embassy had issued a security alert on Saturday, warning of a "credible threat of mass casualties" at the Tsaritsyno Museum Park. This popular tourist destination, comprising a palace and vast gardens, was temporarily closed after the warning.

The US embassy advised people to avoid the area and stated it was coordinating with Russian authorities. The FSB expressed gratitude to the US for the information, noting that investigators are considering legal action against the suspect.
This incident follows a previous US warning to Russia in March 2024, weeks before a terrorist attack at a Moscow concert hall killed over 140 people.
